title: Why slices matter
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" aria-label="A circle cut into eight equal slices with one slice highlighted" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M150,90 L199.5,40.5 A70,70 0 0 0 150.0,20.0 Z" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity="0.3" stroke="none"/><circle cx="150" cy="90" r="70"/><path d="M150,90 L220.0,90.0" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L199.5,40.5" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L150.0,20.0" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L100.5,40.5" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L80.0,90.0" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L100.5,139.5" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L150.0,160.0" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M150,90 L199.5,139.5" stroke-width="1"/><text x="240" y="40" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">one slice</text><text x="240" y="54" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">= one sector</text></svg>
back: Archimedes is credited with cutting a circle into thin slices and rearranging them into a near-rectangle: that is why the area is $\pi r^2$.

title: Sector
back: Two radii and an arc. Minor sector has angle θ; the major sector has 360° − θ.

title: Segment
back: A chord and an arc. Minor segment = sector − triangle OAB.

title: Area of a sector
back: The fraction $\dfrac{\theta}{360}$ of the whole circle.

title: Length of an arc
back: The same fraction of the circumference. Perimeter of the sector: add $2r$.

title: The triangle OAB
back: For 60° the triangle is equilateral; for 120° drop a perpendicular from O.

title: Clock hands
back: Area swept = a sector with the hand as radius.

title: Angles as fractions
back: Spot the fraction and the arithmetic becomes one line.

title: Perimeter of a sector
back: Arc plus the two radii. A quadrant of radius 7 cm: 11 + 14 = 25 cm.
